title: Emergence of a Low-Energy Peak in the Smoothed Absolute Value Circular Dichroism Spectra of Small Helical Gold Nanorods.

sections.heading: Computational Methods
sections.text:
2 Computational Methods To obtain the
optimized Au 24  to Au 56  structures,
we used DFT as implemented in the Gaussian 09 software package. 29  As in our previous DFT studies of small gold
nanorods, 24 − 26  we employed the BP86 functional with a double-ζ
basis set and relativistic effects were included via the LanL2DZ pseudopotential.
The BP86 functional is a widely used gradient-corrected functional,
which combines the exchange term of Becke 30  with the correlation term of Perdew. 31 To obtain the absorption and CD spectra for the optimized
Au 24  to Au 56  structures, we used time-dependent
density
functional theory (TDDFT) as implemented in the Gaussian 09 software
package. 29  See the  SI  for the equations used to generate the spectra. We employed
the long-range-corrected BP86 functional since this correction has
been shown to significantly improve the accuracy of TDDFT calculations. 32 We note that the BP86 functional with
a double-ζ basis set
was used in several recent TDDFT studies of Ag nanoclusters, including
octahedra and icosahedra with comparison to spherical Jellium results, 33  and the geometries and optical spectra of small
Ag clusters (Ag 5  to Ag 12 ) with favorable comparisons
to gas phase spectra. 34  Other studies have
suggested that similar GGA functionals (e.g., PBE) combined with the
LANL2DZ can closely reproduce absorption spectra from rigorous electrodynamics
calculations for small gold clusters. 35 The smoothed spectra were obtained using the standard procedure
(see for example ref ( 9 ) of broadening individual lines with Gaussians as discussed below
with additional details found in the  SI .
